item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) A Young Reality Disruption
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Action

Elevator Pitch: A humanoid male that would accidentally warp-reality if he has too much stress or gets intensely outrageous.

Central Narrative:
SCP-XXXX is a reality-altering humanoid male that is approximately 2 feet tall. The subject will accidentally disrupt reality if mental capacities are largely due to it being the source that can affect their power's capabilities, efficacy, and limitations.

SCP-XXXX was discovered when reports of a paranormal event have occurred, which is shown to be various vehicles falling from the skies. After this was brought to the Foundation, they've located all of the scene witnesses and wipe out their memories. Before doing so, they've asked the witnesses whether they know the cause of the phenomena. The civilians all said that they have no clue what the cause could be. The agents all know that who, or whatever could do so, is somewhere around in that area, as they've asked each people in the area until they've move to the house of a high school male, which eventually claims that he is the caused of the phenomenon. After this, the Foundation has ordered the agents to lied to the boy's parents that he's going to school abroad.

In the interview, SCP-XXXX stated that he discovered his abilities when his father forces him to do a lot of work, which causes him a big amount of stress, also causes him to have a few mental stabilities problem1.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The high-school is a person who lives in a family with a very rigorous father. Due to seeing his son being too joyful and doesn't seem to care whether if he gets in trouble, the father always scolds him non-stop, slowly affecting his mental health.

Additional Notes:

Footnotes
1. Stated that he sometimes talks alone, play with his pencil, walks, run, and jumps around in circles while pulling his hair and talking alone at the same time.

item.title: Forum Crit Team - Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.

In addition, please don't ever put the full text of a draft in a forum post: if you wish to share the draft, the best method is to create a Sandbox Page for it so you can share a link to the draft instead.

item.title: Aerosol SCP
item.content:encoded:
Seeking green light: Yes

Page type: SCP Article

Page layout: Standard SCP format with several addendums and a link to an offset page.

Elevator pitch: The SCP is an anomalous aerosol created by the Manna Charitable Foundation with the intention of reducing the Earth's temperature to halt or reduce global warming by reflecting the Sun's rays using anomalously enhanced sulfur dioxide which are designed to last longer and grow even larger by abosrbing Co2 in the atmosphere. The conprocs for the first iteration states that its currently uncontained and personal assigned are to work on either containing it or lessen its negative effects, as well as preventing the public from learning its anomalous effects.

In the second iteration, the conprocs states its the cause of an active GK-Class "Ozone destruction" scenario and while they are working on to stop by spreading alkaline all across the atmosphere, their unsure if it'll work or not due to the magnitude of the SCP.

Central narrative: A long time ago, the MCF was working on Project Sunna to try and fix global warming as its directly/indirectly responsible for a lot of bad things happening in the world, with funding from not only some governments but also anomaloud GoIs. Its the biggest project MCF has created.

They then released it via planes into the atmosphere which worked for a while; however, as years gone by, the ozone became severely damaged in some parts of the world to the point where thousands are dying. As the SCP Foundation is trying to stop it, the MCF however have fallen and received a shit ton of backlash for this.

Hook: While it maybe another one of those MCF articles where they try to do good things, only to end in disaster this one however takes it to another, global scale where the MCF really fucked up.

Notes: I need someone to help fact check these things to make sure if at least some of it correct.

item.title: Re: Origami Brain
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

a middle aged artist with a degenerative brain disease desperate to understand how the brain works and how to fix her own

As much as I like this as a character motivation, it feels really out of place in a story about origami brains: like, even though it teleports brains to her, it also damages them in a way that almost certainly means she can't get any further insight from them; and it just…feels like it'd be a lot more useful for her to like…get the brains without damaging them? Ideally without even necessarily killing people?

A field agent stationed at a hospital notices something strange on an autopsy report: the deceased person had no brain and no signs of how it was taken

this phrasing kinda implies that the person carrying out the autopsy doesn't notice it was strange? Like the whole way this unfolds kinda implies that somehow people don't notice this happening and it feels…idk, weirdly unsubtle? Like, it feels like death from your brain disappearing would feel… unexpected enough even in a hospital that they'd have to do autopsies and the absence of the brain there feels like a major detail worth flagging?

Iunno, I'm really torn on this as a whole now: the whole angle of the villain is something that really resonates with me and which I really dig; but a lot of what they end up doing and how it works feels…iffy to me to the point where I'm not sure I could suspend my disbelief through the draft.

item.title: Re: Ms. G. Lass
item.content:encoded:
Hm. I'm going to make a really radical suggestion here: this should be a tale. This feels like you're really trying to tell this deeply personal, highly emotional tale of what happens to a Foundation researcher assigned to work with this, and the effect it has on their mental health; and I think that could really work, particularly considering how easily this SCP can escape. But not as a SCP: where the therapy details and the intimate personal feelings of the researcher would feel extremely out of place. Instead, doing this as a tale, likely from the perspective of the researcher but possibly from the perspective of they're therapist or something, would really allow you to convey the emotional turmoil a lot better.

Equally, you're welcome to see if a different reviewer would appreciate this more: it's very possible the idea just doesn't sit right with me personally rather than it being flawed.

item.title: "Man of None"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre (Optional): Horror / Drama / Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): It'll begin as a standardized SCP document, listing the object class, containment procedures, etc etc. The bulk of the article, however, will be inside of the addendum - the interviews, more specifically.

Elevator Pitch: A man under the affect of a seeming "curse". Anyone who verbally confirms any relationship between them and the man dies within the next 24 hours in an unspeakably horrific way, varying from person to person.

Central Narrative: Man of None", a concept I had for an SCP, is a seemingly regular man with a personal love for technology. However, what is strange is the fact anyone who verbally recognizes a relationship between the speaker and the object are killed within 24 hours in an unspeakably painful way. While this may seem as if it's simply for the shock factor of gore and horrific deaths, there's a much darker thing behind it.
He wants to die, however due to the nature of the SCP Foundation his death would be something which would not be wanted. So, they contain him and give him psychological treatment (of course on a very strict regiment), however it never helps. With plenty of research, the only way which suicide patients are helped is via forming relationships with those who help them. And, any relationship with him causes horrific death. So, he's left alone in the world. All that people will call him is an object. They will not say he's their "friend". Not a "loved one". "Family", "enemy", any of the sort is never heard from them.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The man, due to irrelevant trauma, has developed [REDACTED] disorder - which, with hints throughout the article, would be Borderline Personality Disorder. He is absolutely desperate for some form of recognition, approval, or relationship between another human. However, due to the nature of his "curse", he's unable to. This plays to one of the largest human fears of being truly alone. He goes through phases of being desperate for someone to tell him that they care for him in some form, and phases of attempting to hide from others so they don't die a horrific death. He's seen numerous of the things which he's caused, which leaves a permanent trauma to him.

Additional Notes: I'm horrific when it comes to formatting first of all, so if I've messed this up please tell me. I'd like criticism on the entire thing really.

item.title: SCP Idea Seeks Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

  • Doll of a non-descript female anime figure
  • Causes those nearby to into a near-worship state
  • Demands paltry tribute to stay sated
  • The character is unable to be described, named, nor the anime she is from
  • Individuals under the effect feel compelled to talk about her, discussing objective traits like beauty, coolness, etc.
  • When asked, individuals under the effect will reflect questions such as 'YOU don't know HER?' 'I can't believe you'd have to ask me that; a REAL fan would know.'
  • The doll manifested due to a natural proclivity for 'otaku' obsession.
  • The doll represents a void of concept, it can never be fully filled as an idea, so it seeks material items to sate itself.
  • The student discovered the figure and gradually became a classic case of neglecting himself in favor of the idol, pushing people away while lording over them how great his new obsession was.

Central Narrative:

The doll exists in such a way that it compels those nearby to give it small tokens, with no discernable pattern as to what that item needs to be. It prefers to be above eye level on a shelf. The doll was found in a college dorm closet whose occupant began failing out due to offering term papers and other collegiate supplies. Initially thinking that the student was a hoarder, not much thought was given to the situation until the closet was forcefully cleaned and the student's roommate was found bound, malnourished, and near-death within the mass, assumed to be given as tribute when the student did not have anything else to give.

To remain generally inert, the item must receive a tribute every 2-3 days. However, a note from Foundation management has requested that office supplies no longer be offered due to the supply closet constantly needing to be restocked. The longer the doll goes without tribute, the stronger its pull.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
The doll possesses both memetic and antimemetic properties, compelling those under its effect to want to talk about her all the time but unable to physically describe any aspect that would give her characterization.

I'm also extremely conflicted because a lot of this plot feels like it'd work best as a tale centred around one of them repeating the mission over and over again, especially since the Foundation involvement here seems to be uh completely minimal? item.title: A genetics enhancement lab
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Creepy
Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP article, but the plot advances in dialogs between researchers.

Elevator Pitch: The SCP itself is just a glass cage. When you put a specimen inside it, it "reverts" to a single-celled egg, allowing for genetic modification. It will then grow back to the same specimen, but hundreds of generations later, accounting for the modifications brought to it (or not, if there wasn't any).

Central Narrative: The story is based around a doctor and her researcher who tries to understand the SCP, but more importantly what the previous owner was trying to do with it, and what happened to him.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The SCP revolves around damaged notes from the previous owner, describing a few of his experiments, and his downfall. Of course, most of the notes are missing.

item.content:encoded:
+ Cope Crit

Okay, let's see what we have…

A branch of anomalous female humanoid creatures dating back to 150 AD. In childbirth, and the creature she births brings a new anomalous effect. This SCP grows at a rate similar to a human being, but once reaching the year of 29, regardless of contact with any males or injections, she will begin to experience the stages of child birth at a rapid pace, giving birth 3 hours later, and self-terminating. Each generation is only female, and contains one or more anomalous power.

What exactly happens if a male does interact with the female in sexual acts? Does it change how the child is birthed or no?

A linear narrative; The capture of the SCP, attempts to contain each generation, attempts to try to stop the birth process, attempted force abortions, subsequent failures, and the learning of how this SCP functions on a deeper level.

How many of them are there? Is the generation all in one place or spread out across the earth? How does the generation react to this? Do they all have the same opinion or vastly differ?

Each female born from this line carries one or more strong anomalous powers, such as the ability to create and snuff out fires, the ability to warp reality, or the ability to instantly terminate any creature that is in it's area when angry. The seemingly randomness of anomalous power after birth leaving to a constant struggle in contain each generation, and changing of the classification of the SCP.

Okay, now does the powers come at random, or can they be predicted depending on the mother that birthed them?

Overall Thoughts: I honestly can't get X-Men out of my head. Sounds like a different version of mutants. That doesn't mean you shouldn't explore this however. My biggest concern is the creativity of the narrative. You did say it was linear, but it seems to have no unique twist to it. I suggest you talk with a butterfly or more experienced reviewer for this. A guide I can also recommend is how to write a Humanoid. It's highly advised to try not to write one as your first SCP, but by all means, if you would like to, do so. It's what I'm doing. Best of luck to you! I hope your idea soars high!

A single branch of anomalous female humanoid creatures dating back to 150 AD. The creature she births brings a new anomalous effect. This SCP grows at a rate similar to a human being, but once reaching the year of 29, regardless of contact with any males or injections, she will begin to experience the stages of child birth at a rapid pace, giving birth 3 hours later, and self-terminating. Each generation is only female, and contains one or more anomalous power.

Central Narrative:
A linear narrative; The capture of the SCP, attempts to contain each generation, attempts to try to stop the birth process, attempted force abortions, subsequent failures, attemps at containing the 'reincarnations' of this SCP as they come, and the learning of how this SCP functions on a deeper level.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
Each female born from this line carries one or more strong anomalous powers, such as the ability to create and snuff out fires, the ability to warp reality, or the ability to instantly terminate any creature that is in it's area when angry. The seemingly randomness of anomalous power after birth leaving to a constant struggle in contain each generation, and changing of the classification of the SCP. This SCP is only one familial line, not expanding out towards other families.

item.content:encoded:
[+] Overall
[-] Overall

I am…somewhat torn on this as a whole. There's a lot of charm to it that I like, but it feels a touch unsatisfying as a whole, I think in part because the interview doesn't necessarily go very far and really just serves to convey more about what the SCP is: it feels like this is a whole thing built on the mystery of who the SCP is and in turn the reveal of them being santa, and unfortunately I was lurking in #thecritters when grigori asked about that so I figured it out pretty soon.

I think it works as a whole though, and I would likely upvote this but?

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

No other measures are necessary to successfully and safely contain him in his current state

I'm not necessarily sure that 'successfully' and 'safely' are both necessary here; safely contain to me implies successful but?

SCP-XXX is considered a nomenclative hazard (Eshu Class).

Something like "SCP-XXXX is an Eshu Class nomenclative hazard" might read better here; even if this is the phrasing SCP-4000 uses to refer to it.

However, previous attempts to contain SCP-XXXX per protocol 4000-Eshu have been deemed inadequate.

My personal preference would be for this to continue with e.g. "due to [reason]", namely, where the reasons it's been deemed inadequate are in some way shown.

I'd also lean towards capitalising protocol here and in the next sentence but it's largely a stylistic thing so w/e.

As an additional measure, the entrance of cell B5 is to be reinforced with iron.

I'd lean towards including this as a paragraph on it's own? It feels like it doesn't quite flow from the previous stuff but?

These alterations have been marked for differentiation from the standard formatting.

My personal preference here would be to explicitly say 'marked in blue' over making it blue, though I think it's clear enough without?

SCP-XXXX has knowledge of the name, middle name (if any), and surnames of all people it comes into contact with.

I feel like '…knowledge of the full name of all…' would be clearer, with like, middle/surnames being possibly mentioned in a footnote; though that feels unnecessary.

access granted

I'd probably capitalise this (Access Granted).

SCP-XXX was discovered during a performance of the 4000-Halloway procedure.

Minor note but this placeholder has only 3 X's so I'd probably add an extra just to ensure you don't miss it when changing the placeholder into a number.

which resulted in the appearance of SCP-XXXX in the chimney rather than an entrance to the the place of the nameless oddities.

this phrasing is a little ambiguous as to whether you mean "SCP-XXXX should have appeared in the entrance to the place of the nameless oddities but instead appeared in the chimney" or (more likely) "the entrance to the place of the nameless oddities should have appeared but instead SCP-XXXX appeared in the chimney"

This is believed to be due to the cultural association toof the epithet in question.

The following is an interview conducted on June 20th 1996.

This date is meaningless to us because we don't know when it is in relation to the discovery of the SCP: it could be two days later, it could be two hundred years later or it could be thirty days before.

however two members of security personnel were present beside the chamber entrance for emergency assistance

SCP-XXXX, I actually came to ask you a few questions. We want to know how you differ from the others like you.

Addressing the SCP directly here like this feels a little odd: like, there's only two people in the room, so it seems unnecessary for her to do this?

I see now, I see, you mean ██████.

See, this feels like it's hiding 'Santa' but it's a letter too long for that so I'm not sure if I'm wrong or this is a mistake?

Well, this clearly isn't the case for you, SCP-XXXX.

But, one makes duedo if they areone is to survive.

they to one here to keep the pronoun consistent

SCP-XXXX laughs

SCP-XXXX: I don't believe I ever said such a thing

Okay so this visually appears like it has an extra line but reading the page source, it's that none of the others do properly, probably because one of your ">"'s doesn't have a space after it?

(It's generally easier to wrap long things like this between "[[div class="blockquote"]]" and "[[/div]]", since it doesn't have awkward stuff like this)

Footnote 5. holly

item.title: SCP *PLACE HOLDER NUMBER* The Bee movie.
item.content:encoded:
For context before we get into the meat of this thread, I was inspired to write this because I've often heard the bee movie be described as a collective fever dream, I feel like it could fit into the joke scp category, but I think with more tweaking it could be a full fledged article.

Scp 9999 The Bee movie.

Object class: Safe.

Special containment procedures:

Due to the circumstances surrounding SCP 9999 full scale containment as of this moment is both impossible and unnecessary. Personnel are instead instructed to avoid viewing SCP 9999, MTF-PHI 22 “Fever Dreamers” is to be alerted to any devices reported to contain a recording of SCP 9999, recordings are to be either destroyed or given directly to Director McKinley for [DATAEXPUNGED]. If any personnel should happen to view SCP 9999 they are instructed to avoid telling others about it or posting about it on social media in order to attempt to slow the spread of its anomalous effects.

Description:

SCP 9999 is the official designation for a viral phenomenon which causes the victim to hallucinate having viewed a computer animated movie from 2007 called The Bee Movie which stars comedian Jerry Seinfeld. Those affected usually have wildly different experiences in regards to SCP 9999, with some reporting that the film they watched was a romantic comedy, while others report that the film they watched was a surreal horror film, in spite of this however four factors remain constant.

Number one: the main character is always voiced by Jerry Seinfeld.

Number two: the main character will attempt to sue the human race over their consumption of honey.

Number three: the love interest of the main character will always be human.

Number four: the film will always end with The main character and the love interest opening a joined flower shop/law firm.

Although the foundation has managed to create a ‘dummy film’ and amnestise most of those who have been affected by SCP 9999, there remain a few affected individuals who further propagate the effects of SCP 9999.

item.title: Re: The Spire - needs greenlights
item.content:encoded:
In terms of how it works, it looks pretty solid. The two basic problems are the hook and the why.

The Why: It would be interesting why the reality warper created this tool. Sure, there's the possibility of it happened randomly, but that's no fun; there has to be a reason for why it exists, be it a tool, a weapon, or even a puzzle. In short, there has to be a reason why it exists. In that regard, it would be interesting to see what the others looked like and see if there was some sort of pattern to them.

The Hook: Testing would have been discontinued once the majority of rules were figured out so as to avoid it teleporting. What you need is a reason for people to care about it, what it says about the SPC-U as a whole, or just what kind of niche it fills. In short, why testing was discontinued just isn't interesting when the reason is somewhat obvious, and if it isn't obvious then it needs to be stated.

There just needs to be a reason for people to care about the item.
